meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Elegance is the only beauty that never fades'?
meta.ogDescription: Pinned on Audrey Hepburn across the web, yet traceable to no primary source and absent from Wikiquote. Likely a modern aphorism, not her words.

answer.label: Not documented for Audrey Hepburn — an unsourced saying
answer.sourceLine: Credited to Hepburn on countless quote sites, yet it turns up in none of her documented films, interviews, letters, or books, and it is absent even from Wikiquote’s Audrey Hepburn entry ↗. No primary source pins this exact wording to her, and no alternative author is documented — so the attribution is best treated as unverified.

source.excerpt: Elegance is the only beauty that never fades.
trail: The line saturates quote aggregators such as Goodreads ↗ and QuoteFancy ↗, always credited to Hepburn but never with a film, date, or page.
Fan sites that discuss it, like Quoteikon ↗, present it as hers while citing no documented occasion for her saying it.
It does not appear anywhere in Wikiquote’s Audrey Hepburn page ↗ — not in the sourced, attributed, or misattributed sections.
The name occasionally floated as an alternative, John Ruskin ↗, is not supported either: the exact wording is absent from his documented works.
source.excerptNote: Repeated verbatim across quote aggregators and social posts, always credited to Hepburn but never with a traceable source.
source.rightsNote: Because no first documented source or author can be established for this exact wording, no copyright status can honestly be asserted. If it is a 20th- or 21st-century aphorism — as the evidence suggests — it would likely be in copyright to whoever first wrote it, but that person is unknown.

author.name: Audrey Hepburn
author.heading: Audrey Hepburn
author.bio: Audrey Hepburn was a screen icon of the 1950s and ’60s — Roman Holiday, Sabrina, Breakfast at Tiffany’s — and later a devoted UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador. Her name became shorthand for grace and understated elegance, which is precisely why polished maxims about beauty and style gravitate to her regardless of whether she ever spoke them. No record shows she originated this particular line.

misattribution.heading: Often misattributed
misattribution.intro: This is a textbook “halo” attribution: an elegant-sounding aphorism about beauty and elegance, pinned to the 20th century’s foremost symbol of both. The credit is repeated so often it looks authoritative — but it rests on nothing documented.

items.why: Attached to her on Goodreads ↗, QuoteFancy ↗ and countless social posts, yet tied to no film, interview, letter, or book — and absent from Wikiquote’s Hepburn entry ↗.
The Victorian critic wrote extensively on beauty, so his name occasionally attaches to the line — but this exact wording does not appear in his documented quotes ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: No primary source supports either name. Until someone locates the words in Hepburn’s actual speech or writing — or in an identifiable original author — this is best read as an undocumented modern saying ↗, not a verified Hepburn quote.

context.heading: Why it sticks to her
lead: Hepburn’s public image — the little black dress, the poise, the restraint — made her the natural magnet for any tidy epigram equating elegance with lasting beauty. The sentiment fits her so neatly that few readers stop to ask for a source.

That fit is exactly the warning sign. Feel-good lines migrate toward famous, on-brand names, and the more ‘obviously’ a quote suits someone, the more worth checking whether they ever actually said it. Here, the paper trail runs out.
context.pull: The better it fits the icon, the more it needs a source — and this one has none.
